name: process
summary: A Node.js-compatible implementation of the core `process` module
description:
Titanium provides a number of shims and ports of core Node.js module functionality.

This module is intended to provide a Node-compatible port of the `process` core module.

More details on the Node.js API can be found in their [process module documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/process.html)

Note that this particular shim has many unimplemented, no-op, or unsupported APIs and events.

The `process` object is a global that provides information about, and control over, the current Node.js process. As a global, it is always available to Node.js applications without using `require()`. It can also be explicitly accessed using `require()`:

``` javascript
const process = require('process');
```

properties.name: arch
properties.summary:
Returns the operating system CPU architecture for which the binary was compiled. Possible values are return `'arm'`, `'arm64'`, `'ia32'`, `'x64'`, `'mips'`, and `'unknown'`.

The return value is equivalent to [os.arch](api:os#arch). Relates strongly to [Titanium.Platform.architecture](api:Titanium.Platform#architecture).

properties.name: argv
properties.summary:
The `process.argv` property returns an array containing the command-line arguments passed when the Node.js process was launched.
The first element will be `process.execPath`. See [process.argv0](api:process#argv0) if access to the original value of `argv[0]` is needed.
The second element will be the path to the JavaScript file being executed.
The remaining elements will be any additional command-line arguments.

properties.name: argv0
properties.summary: The `process.argv0` property stores a read-only copy of the original value of `argv[0]` passed when Node.js starts.

properties.name: channel
properties.summary: Always `undefined` in Titanium.

properties.name: config
properties.summary: Always `{}` in Titanium.

properties.name: connected
properties.summary: Always `false` in Titanium.

properties.name: debugPort
properties.summary: The port used by the debugger when enabled.

properties.name: env
properties.summary:
This is an object whose keys are environment variable names and whose values are the related environment variable values.

In Titanium, we will pass along environment variables from the system/CLI to the app for `'development'` builds,
*but will not do so for `'production'` builds!*

properties.name: execArgv
properties.summary: Always `[]` in Titanium.

properties.name: execPath
properties.summary: Always `''` in Titanium.

properties.name: exitCode
properties.summary: Unused in Titanium.

properties.name: noDeprecation
properties.summary: The `process.noDeprecation` property indicates whether the `--no-deprecation` flag is set on the current Node.js process. See the documentation for the `'warning'` event and the `emitWarning()` method for more information about this flag's behavior.

properties.name: pid
properties.summary: The `process.pid` property returns the PID of the process. Always returns `0` in Titanium.

properties.name: platform
properties.summary: Equivalent to [Titanium.Platform.osname](api:Titanium.Platform#osname)

properties.name: ppid
properties.summary: The `process.ppid` property returns the PID of the parent of the current process. Always returns `0` in Titanium.

properties.name: stderr
properties.summary: The `process.stderr` property returns a stream connected to `stderr`.

properties.name: stdout
properties.summary: The `process.stdout` property returns a stream connected to `stdout`.

properties.name: throwDeprecation
properties.summary: The initial value of `process.throwDeprecation` indicates whether the `--throw-deprecation` flag is set on the current Node.js process. process.throwDeprecation is mutable, so whether or not deprecation warnings result in errors may be altered at runtime. See the documentation for the `'warning'` event and the `emitWarning()` method for more information.

properties.name: title
properties.summary: Equivalent to [Titanium.App.name](api:Titanium.App#name)

properties.name: traceDeprecation
properties.summary: The `process.traceDeprecation` property indicates whether the `--trace-deprecation` flag is set on the current Node.js process. See the documentation for the `'warning'` event and the `emitWarning()` method for more information about this flag's behavior.

properties.name: version
properties.summary: Equivalent to [Titanium.version](api:Titanium#version)

properties.name: versions
properties.summary: An object containing version information for included dependencies

methods.name: binding
methods.summary: This is not intended as user-facing API and will throw an `Error` if invoked.

methods.name: chdir
methods.summary: This is unsupported on Titanium and will throw an `Error` if invoked.

methods.name: cpuUsage
methods.summary: Returns a dummy object with `0`-ed out values.

methods.name: cwd
methods.summary: Returns the value of `__dirname` on Titanium.

methods.name: dlopen
methods.summary: This is unsupported on Titanium and will throw an `Error` if invoked.

methods.name: emitWarning
methods.summary: The `process.emitWarning()` method can be used to emit custom or application specific process warnings. These can be listened for by adding a handler to the `'warning'` event.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary: When `warning` is a `String`, `type` is the name to use for the type of warning being emitted.

inlined.name: EmitWarningOptions
inlined.summary: An abstract type for the options that may be passed to [process.emitWarning](api:process#emitWarning)().

properties.name: code
properties.summary: A unique identifier for the warning instance being emitted.

properties.name: ctor
properties.summary: When `warning` is a `String`, `ctor` is an optional function used to limit the generated stack trace.

properties.name: detail
properties.summary: Additional text to include with the error.

properties.name: type
properties.summary: When `warning` is a `String`, `type` is the name to use for the type of warning being emitted.

parameters.name: code
parameters.summary: A unique identifier for the warning instance being emitted.

parameters.name: ctor
parameters.summary: When `warning` is a `String`, `ctor` is an optional function used to limit the generated stack trace.

methods.name: exit
methods.summary: This is unsupported on Titanium and will throw an `Error` if invoked.

methods.name: umask
methods.summary: No-op on Titanium. Will always return `0`.

methods.name: uptime
methods.summary:
The `process.uptime()` method returns the number of seconds the current Node.js process has been running.

The return value includes fractions of a second. Use `Math.floor()` to get whole seconds.

events.name: uncaughtException
events.summary: The `'uncaughtException'` event is emitted when an uncaught JavaScript exception bubbles all the way back to the event loop.

properties.name: err
properties.summary: The uncaught exception.

events.name: warning
events.summary: The `'warning'` event is emitted whenever Node.js emits a `process` warning.

properties.name: warning
properties.summary: The warning thrown.
